summary: Calculates first, second, or third derivatives of input channels, commonly converting position to speed or acceleration.
key_concepts: Slope CHOP calculates the slope or derivative of input channels.
When the input represents position, the default slope output can be interpreted as speed.
Type selects first derivative slope, second derivative acceleration, or acceleration of slope.
Method chooses previous/current, current/next, or previous/next sample pairs; previous/current is the realtime-safe method.
Slope per Sample applies derivative calculation to each sample of multi-sample channels.
Slope CHOP can pair with Speed CHOP to edit speed or acceleration and reconstruct position, but the original starting position must be restored separately.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Slope, acceleration, or acceleration of slope

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Previous/current, current/next, or previous/next sample method

key_params.name: slopesamples
key_params.note: Apply slope per sample for multi-sample channels

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Default use converts position-like channels to speed-like channels.
Previous/current is the only method applicable in realtime applications because it does not require future samples.
Previous/next is smoother for offline curves but needs samples on both sides.
Slope removes absolute starting position information; use Speed CHOP constants or offsets when integrating back.
Units can be interpreted per sample, frame, or second based on CHOP settings.
Use with Speed CHOP to edit speed or acceleration and reconstruct position.
Current/next and previous/next methods use future samples, so they are not appropriate for realtime-only analysis.
